questions.q: What problem does a Snowflake Stream solve, compared to a homemade watermark column?
options: It tracks inserts, updates, and deletes on a table natively, without you maintaining a watermark column that can miss updates or can't see deletes
It makes queries run on a larger warehouse automatically
It replaces the need for any table in Snowflake
It encrypts all data in a table automatically
questions.explain: A watermark column is homemade bookkeeping that breaks on updates that don't touch it and can't detect deletes at all; a Stream tracks all DML changes natively.

questions.q: What does `METADATA$ISUPDATE = TRUE` indicate on a row returned from a stream?
options: That row is part of a DELETE+INSERT pair representing an UPDATE, since Snowflake has no separate UPDATE action
The row was never actually changed
The row will be automatically deleted soon
The stream itself is about to expire
questions.explain: Snowflake represents an UPDATE as a paired DELETE of the old row version and INSERT of the new one, both flagged METADATA$ISUPDATE = TRUE.

questions.q: Does a plain `SELECT * FROM my_stream;` used just to look at the data consume the stream?
options: No — only a DML statement that reads from the stream and commits advances what the stream considers already-seen
Yes — any SELECT against a stream immediately empties it
Streams cannot be queried with SELECT at all
It depends on the warehouse size
questions.explain: A plain SELECT to peek is safe and doesn't consume the stream; only a committing DML statement that reads from it (like an INSERT ... SELECT or MERGE) advances its offset.

questions.q: What does `METADATA$ACTION` tell you about a row returned by a stream?
options: Whether that row represents an INSERT or a DELETE
The exact timestamp the table was created
The name of the warehouse that ran the query
The total row count in the base table
questions.explain: METADATA$ACTION is one of INSERT or DELETE, describing what happened to that captured row version.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use code cards instead of a Snowsight screenshot?
options: Because a Stream is a SQL/DDL object with no dedicated Snowsight visual, and no real Streams-focused UI screenshot could be found after searching Snowflake's own Quickstarts
Because screenshots are never allowed in this course
Because Streams do not actually exist in Snowsight
Because code cards render faster than images
